channel.title: The Awesome Ledger — awesome-annual-security-reports
channel.description: New entries across the GitHub awesome ecosystem, diffed nightly.

item.title: Plume — via awesome-annual-security-reports
item.description: Residential Proxy Malware (2026) - Examines the proliferation of residential proxy networks within Android applications, highlighting how sideloaded streaming tools quietly enroll compromised devices into monetization frameworks without user consent. Key findings reveal that 100% of analyzed installations of the AppLinked tool silently deploy the Netway software development kit, leveraging background services and native proxy binaries to poll command and control servers every 5 minutes while maintaining persistent outbound connections through reverse tunnels.

item.title: Infoblox — via awesome-annual-security-reports
item.description: DNS Threat Landscape Report (2026) - Examines the escalating scale of industrialized cybercrime and automated threat infrastructures through telemetry analysis of trillions of DNS queries. Key findings reveal that 22 percent of over 120 million newly registered domains were weaponized, while scam-related domains surged by 62 percent year over year alongside a 158 percent increase in enterprise DNS queries directed toward artificial intelligence applications.

item.title: HardenStance — via awesome-annual-security-reports
item.description: Briefing on Enea Voice Firewall (2025) - Examines the deployment and operational efficacy of telecommunication voice firewalls designed to mitigate caller identification spoofing and fraudulent communications. Key findings reveal a 90 percent reduction in incoming scam calls following commercial implementation alongside the capability to process mobile networks accounting for at least 80 percent of total voice traffic.

item.title: HardenStance — via awesome-annual-security-reports
item.description: Telco Strategies for Consumer Security (2026) - Investigates global telecommunication operator strategies and investments in consumer cybersecurity software. Key findings indicate that global spending reached $441 million in 2025, which amounts to less than 0.1% of the $442 billion total annual cost of scams estimated by the Global Anti-Scam Alliance.

item.title: Snyk — via awesome-annual-security-reports
item.description: Cloud Native Application Security Report (2026) - Examines the state of cloud native application security, highlighting deployment practices and vulnerability management trends. Key findings reveal that over 56 percent of organizations experienced a security incident involving misconfigurations or known unpatched vulnerabilities, while more than 72 percent of fully automated development teams successfully find and remediate critical security issues in under one week.

item.title: Saviynt — via awesome-annual-security-reports
item.description: AI Identity Risk Report (2026) - Examines the security risks and governance challenges associated with the rapid enterprise adoption of artificial intelligence identities and autonomous agents. Key findings reveal that 92% of organizations lack full visibility into their artificial intelligence identities, while 86% currently fail to enforce formal access policies for these autonomous systems.

item.title: Redhat — via awesome-annual-security-reports
item.description: State of Cloud Native Security (2026) - Examines the state of cloud-native security and governance maturity across modern enterprise environments. Key insights reveal that 97% of organizations experienced at least one security incident in the past year, while 79% report that generative artificial intelligence is creating new security challenges despite 59% lacking documented internal usage policies.

item.title: PDI — via awesome-annual-security-reports
item.description: Cyber Threat Landscape Report Q1 (2026) - Analyzes the cyber threat landscape for the first quarter of 2026 by examining more than four trillion security events collected across global environments. Key findings reveal a staggering 247 percent surge in exploit activity alongside a 61 percent year over year increase in ransomware attacks driven by expanding access paths and edge device vulnerabilities.

item.title: MixMode — via awesome-annual-security-reports
item.description: Cloud Security Report (2026) - Investigates the current state of cloud security and multi-cloud deployment strategies, detailing the challenges organizations face in securing modern digital environments. Key findings reveal that 75% of security professionals are extremely or very concerned about cloud security, while 70% continue to rely on legacy solutions like information event management tools that struggle to provide adequate functionality in dynamic cloud architectures.

item.title: Hughes — via awesome-annual-security-reports
item.description: Secure Network Access Report (2025) - Examines the state of secure network access, evaluating the adoption trends of technologies like secure access service edge and zero trust models across modern hybrid enterprises. Key findings reveal that 52% of organizations struggle most with securing remote network connectivity, while 48% cite integration with existing systems as the primary barrier to adopting advanced cloud security solutions.

item.title: Gurucul — via awesome-annual-security-reports
item.description: Pulse AI SOC Report (2025) - Examines the state of artificial intelligence adoption within security operations centers, focusing on threat detection, workflow automation, and analyst burnout. Key findings reveal that 87% of organizations are currently deploying, piloting, or evaluating artificial intelligence tools, while 60% of adopters have successfully cut investigation times by at least 25%.

item.title: Fortinet — via awesome-annual-security-reports
item.description: Data Security Report (2025) - Examines the current state of enterprise data protection and reveals that 77% of organizations experienced insider-related data loss over an 18-month period. Key findings indicate that 72% of companies lack visibility into how users interact with sensitive data across cloud and endpoint environments, while 41% suffered damages between $1 million and $10 million from their most significant incident.

item.title: Fortinet — via awesome-annual-security-reports
item.description: Email Security Report (2026) - Examines the state of email security defenses and organizational readiness against evolving email-based threat vectors. Findings reveal that 75 percent of security professionals consider integrating email tools into broader security infrastructure crucial.

item.title: Fortinet — via awesome-annual-security-reports
item.description: Insider Risk Report (2025) - Examines the state of enterprise insider risk management and highlights current operational maturity levels, tool effectiveness, and visibility gaps across modern hybrid environments. Key insights reveal that 77% of organizations experienced insider driven data loss in the past 18 months, while 72% lack visibility into how users interact with sensitive data across endpoints and cloud platforms.

item.title: Darktrace — via awesome-annual-security-reports
item.description: Remote Workforce Security Report (2026) - Examines the cybersecurity risks and operational challenges introduced by the sudden shift to a remote workforce across global organizations. Key findings reveal that 80% of security professionals are moderately to extremely concerned about remote work risks, with 71% identifying phishing and 61% identifying malware as their primary threat vectors.

item.title: Cogility — via awesome-annual-security-reports
item.description: Insider Risk Report (2025) - Examines the state of insider risk management and modern data security challenges across corporate networks. Key findings reveal that 92 percent of recent incidents lacked proper access controls, while 96 percent of organizations feel confident despite 70 percent experiencing a breach.

item.title: Balbix — via awesome-annual-security-reports
item.description: State of Security Posture Report (2026) - Examines the state of security posture management and reveals that cybersecurity teams struggle to measure and improve their defenses as organizations transition to the cloud. Key findings indicate that 62% of organizations lack confidence in their overall security posture and are unable to quantify cyber risk in monetary units, while 86% identify phishing and ransomware as their primary security threats.

item.title: OpenSystems — via awesome-annual-security-reports
item.description: SASE Report (2026) - Examines the adoption of managed secure access service edge and zero trust architectures across hybrid enterprise environments. Key findings reveal that 76% of organizations cite heightened security requirements as the primary driver for replacing legacy virtual private networks, while 48% struggle with the operational burden of running parallel access models.

item.title: Netskope — via awesome-annual-security-reports
item.description: AI Security Report (2026) - Examines the state of artificial intelligence security and governance based on a comprehensive survey of 1253 cybersecurity professionals. Key findings reveal that while 90% of organizations increased their security budgets, 94% still report critical visibility gaps and only 7% have successfully implemented real-time policy enforcement.

item.title: Netskope — via awesome-annual-security-reports
item.description: VPNs Under Siege Report (2026) - Examines the state of remote access security and the transition from legacy virtual private networks and network access control systems to zero trust network access. Key findings reveal that 56 percent of organizations experienced a virtual private network related security incident in the past year, while 76 percent now consider replacing legacy network access control solutions a high priority.

item.title: Netskope — via awesome-annual-security-reports
item.description: Unified Data Security (2026) - Examines the state of data security tooling and visibility gaps across enterprise environments, focusing on the challenges of tracking sensitive information as it moves into artificial intelligence workflows. Key findings reveal that 58 percent of organizations operate eleven or more security tools while only 7 percent maintain a fully unified stack, and 98 percent now use artificial intelligence despite just 14 percent enforcing consistent inline controls.

item.title: MITRE — via awesome-annual-security-reports
item.description: Threat Informed Defense Report (2026) - Examines the state of threat-informed defense and industry adoption of the MITRE framework through a comprehensive survey of security professionals. Key findings reveal that while 82 percent of respondents know about the framework, only 8 percent use it regularly, and 84 percent lack a thorough mapping of their defenses to its techniques.

item.title: Imperva — via awesome-annual-security-reports
item.description: API Security Threat Report (2026) - Examines API security threats and token handling risks across 32,725 endpoints and 1,104 customer accounts. Key findings reveal that nearly 40% of endpoints carry multiple authentication risks simultaneously, with sensitive data appearing in 49.8% of detections and expired-token access experiencing a 70% relative increase.

item.title: HPE — via awesome-annual-security-reports
item.description: Zero Trust Security Report (2026) - Examines the state of Zero Trust adoption and the execution gap across modern hybrid enterprises. Key findings reveal that while 82 percent of surveyed organizations view Universal Zero Trust Network Access as essential, only 17 percent have fully implemented it, with 56 percent citing employee over-privilege as the leading contributor to unauthorized access risks.

item.title: HPE — via awesome-annual-security-reports
item.description: VPN Exposure Report (2025) - Examines the current state of VPN security and the shift toward modern remote access alternatives based on a comprehensive survey of industry professionals. Key findings reveal that 48% of organizations have experienced a VPN-related cyberattack, while 72% maintain between two and five different VPN services, significantly expanding their enterprise attack surface.

item.title: Fortinet — via awesome-annual-security-reports
item.description: Web Application Security Report (2026) - Examines the security posture of web applications and APIs in the context of artificial intelligence adoption, highlighting a widening readiness gap between modernization and operational control. Key findings reveal that 74% of organizations observed an increase in artificial intelligence assisted attacks over the past year, while overall security confidence for artificial intelligence integrated applications dropped to 15%.

item.title: Cyberedge — via awesome-annual-security-reports
item.description: Cyber Threat Defense Report (2026) - Examines global IT security postures and threat defense strategies based on responses from 1200 qualified professionals across 17 countries. Key insights reveal that 80.7% of surveyed organizations experienced at least one successful cyberattack in the past year, while 30.4% of those affected suffered six or more breaches.

item.title: Securtas — via awesome-annual-security-reports
item.description: Annual Intelligence Estimate Report (2026) - Examines the global corporate security and risk landscape for 2026, providing comprehensive threat assessments across multiple regional sectors and critical infrastructure domains. Key findings highlight that 100 percent of evaluated strategic drivers require advanced intelligence methodologies to mitigate escalating geopolitical volatility, artificial intelligence disruption, and emerging socioeconomic protest movements.

item.title: Grip — via awesome-annual-security-reports
item.description: SaaS Security Risks Report (2026) - Examines the state of SaaS and artificial intelligence security risks, highlighting how unmanaged enterprise adoption creates critical operational vulnerabilities. Key findings reveal that 100 percent of analyzed organizations operate environments with embedded artificial intelligence components, while 80 percent of documented incidents involve personally identifiable information or customer data.

item.title: Fortinet — via awesome-annual-security-reports
item.description: Cybersecurity Skills Gap Report (2026) - Examines the intersection of artificial intelligence adoption and the global cybersecurity skills shortage across organizations. Key findings reveal that 91% of respondents use or experiment with artificial intelligence-powered security solutions, while 52% report breach costs exceeding one million dollars.

item.title: F5 — via awesome-annual-security-reports
item.description: Office of the CTO Report Continuous API Sprawl (2026) - Examines the rapid expansion and economic impact of application programming interfaces across modern enterprise environments, detailing the primary factors driving continuous digital sprawl. Key findings reveal that the total number of worldwide application programming interfaces is rapidly approaching 200 million, with projections indicating active endpoints could exceed 1 billion by 2031 due to accelerated microservices adoption and continuous development cycles.

item.title: Baird — via awesome-annual-security-reports
item.description: Disruptors (2026) - Examines the landscape of private security and infrastructure software companies, profiling 29 influential market vendors across distinct operational categories. Key findings reveal that 70% of these evaluated organizations specialize in advanced cloud, data, and identity protection platforms to combat modern cyber threats.
